section_summary: This section documents official deliberations and studies between May and September 1949 concerning criminal and civil judicial jurisdiction in occupied Japan. It centers on an extensive February 1948 monograph by the Japanese Foreign Office assessing SCAP directives, court casework, the legal status of Formosans, and Japanese claims for damages inflicted by Allied personnel. Subsequent documents trace proposals by SCAP Legal Section, General Douglas MacArthur, and the Department of the Army to restore concurrent criminal jurisdiction over non-occupation United Nations nationals to Japanese courts, culminating in State Department policy drafting for the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.about: Transmits five copies of a Japanese Foreign Office monograph concerning judicial jurisdiction under Allied occupation.
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits and analyzes a Japanese Foreign Office monograph on judicial jurisdiction, highlighting Formosan nationality questions, conquest and territorial transfer, and unadjudicated Japanese damage claims against occupation personnel.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 281: Japanese Monograph on Questions Concerning Judicial Jurisdiction

subfiles.about: Comprehensive study by the Japanese Foreign Office on the exercise of civil and criminal jurisdiction under Allied occupation directives and related legal issues.
subfiles.summary: This report reviews the implementation and domestic enforcement of SCAP directives on civil and criminal jurisdiction, including Imperial Ordinance No. 311. It provides detailed statistics on civil and economic cases involving United Nations nationals and analyzes difficulties arising from the extraterritorial exemption of Allied nationals. The study focuses heavily on the unsettled legal status of Formosans in Japan and the urgent need for a mechanism to compensate Japanese victims of crimes and accidents caused by Allied personnel.
subfiles.title: Monograph: Questions Concerning Judicial Jurisdiction
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Transmits a GHQ SCAP Legal Section study recommending progressive restoration of Japanese criminal jurisdiction over United Nations nationals.
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits a GHQ SCAP Legal Section study proposing Japanese courts resume criminal jurisdiction over certain United Nations nationals.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 382: Japanese Exercise of Criminal Jurisdiction over United Nations Nationals

subfiles.about: Proposes requesting the Far Eastern Commission to amend policy directives to restore Japanese concurrent criminal jurisdiction over non-occupation United Nations nationals.
subfiles.from: C. R. Liggit, Acting Chief, Legal Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Proposes amending Far Eastern Commission directives to authorize Japanese concurrent criminal jurisdiction over non-occupation United Nations nationals, citing historical occupation precedents and reformed Japanese legal safeguards.
subfiles.title: Legal Section Study: Exercise of Criminal Jurisdiction in Japan
subfiles.to: Judge Advocate Section, Diplomatic Section, Government Section, ESS, G-1, G-2

subfiles.about: Draft radio requesting amendment of directive WCL 38511 to grant Japanese courts concurrent criminal jurisdiction over certain United Nations nationals.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
subfiles.summary: Draft radio requesting JCS amend directive WCL 38511 to authorize Japanese concurrent criminal jurisdiction over non-occupation United Nations nationals.
subfiles.title: Draft Outgoing Message from SCAP to JCS on Exercise of Criminal Jurisdiction in Japan

subfiles.about: Supports General MacArthur's recommendation to permit Japanese courts concurrent criminal jurisdiction over United Nations nationals and urges State to submit a proposal to the FEC.
subfiles.from: Robert R. West, Deputy to Assistant Secretary of the Army
subfiles.summary: Urges the State Department to propose an amendment in the Far Eastern Commission permitting Japanese concurrent criminal jurisdiction over United Nations nationals.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of the Army regarding Amendment of FEC Policy on Criminal Jurisdiction
subfiles.to: W. Walton Butterworth, Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Offers comments and revisions on a draft memorandum concerning criminal jurisdiction in Japan and comparisons with the German Occupation Statute.
subfiles.from: J. W. Auchincloss, GAP, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Comments on draft memorandum regarding criminal jurisdiction over foreigners in Japan, advising against overemphasizing the German Occupation Statute.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Criminal Jurisdiction Over Foreigners in Japan
subfiles.to: Mrs. Alice L. Dunning, NA, Department of State

subfiles.about: Analyzes SCAP's proposal and recommends State Department concurrence with amending FEC policy on criminal jurisdiction, rejecting concurrent jurisdiction in favor of exclusive Japanese jurisdiction over non-excepted categories.
subfiles.from: Niles W. Bond, Officer in Charge of Japanese Affairs (NA)
subfiles.summary: Reviews proposals to restore Japanese criminal jurisdiction over non-occupation United Nations nationals, recommending State support an amended FEC policy while rejecting concurrent jurisdiction to avoid procedural confusion.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Japanese Exercise of Criminal Jurisdiction Over United Nation's Nationals
subfiles.to: W. Walton Butterworth, Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs (FE)

subfiles.about: Draft policy decision authorizing Japanese courts to exercise criminal jurisdiction over United Nations nationals, with specific exceptions for occupation personnel and officials.
subfiles.from: Alice L. Dunning, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Draft policy decision authorizing Japanese courts to exercise criminal jurisdiction over United Nations nationals except occupation forces, official personnel, and dependents.
subfiles.title: Proposed FEC Policy Decision: Exercise of Criminal Jurisdiction in Japan

subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Duplicate file copy of Despatch No. 382 transmitting Legal Section study on restoring Japanese criminal jurisdiction.
